issue.mint_text: Royal Mint (United Kingdom); no mint mark on this issue; date on the ship side

new.story: Ten cents from the East Caribbean States, dated 2004 — pocket money shared by eight Caribbean islands under one dollar and one central bank. The ship is the Golden Hind, the galleon Sir Francis Drake sailed around the world in the 1570s, drawn by Thomas Humphrey Paget; the crowned portrait of Queen Elizabeth the Second on the front is by Ian Rank-Broadley. This is the copper-nickel striking the islands used before switching to lighter steel coins in 2009, made for them at the Royal Mint in Britain. The collection already holds a 2004 strike of this coin recorded earlier from a shorthand note; this is the first one photographed on both sides.
new.notes: Both sides photographed in the holder. Reverse: EAST CARIBBEAN STATES around the Golden Hind, the date after STATES read digit by digit in an enhanced crop as 2-0-0-4, a 10 on each side of the ship, TEN CENTS below. Obverse: QUEEN ELIZABETH THE SECOND around the crowned Rank-Broadley portrait. Correction history, kept on the record: this coin was first filed today as a 2014 steel strike (changes_muse_20261109-1733, withdrawn) — the coin sits rotated in its photo and the faint third digit of the date was misread as a 1; the owner corrected it to 2004 and a fresh enlarged read confirms 2-0-0-4. Two flags for the merge: (1) C159 is also an EC.KM.37 2004 strike, recorded from shorthand with no checkable photos — if that record describes this same physical coin, this specimen duplicates it; flagged rather than assumed either way. (2) The type's stored 2004 issue note says the date is carried on the Elizabeth II obverse; these photos show the date on the ship side, after STATES, so that stored note looks wrong.
